description: Pragmatism is a philosophical school of thought holding that the truth of our theories depends on their practical value. Students will explore the foundations of this deceptively radical view as it emerged in late 19th and early 20th Century America.  And they will follow its more recent development through major innovations in metaphysics, epistemology, ethics, political philosophy, and the philosophy of science. Readings include William James, John Dewey, Richard Rorty, Elizabeth Anderson, and others. Prerequisite: two courses in philosophy, one of which must be either PHIL 235 or PHIL 236 or permission of the department chair.
